clue.text: Dose of medicine from container one in operation required

parts.note: a pot is a container
the Roman numeral for one
a machine in operation is on

explanation.surface: A pharmacist measuring out a dose from a jar during a procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a liquid drink of medicine, a single measured draught of a remedy.

clue.text: Journalists harass crowd

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the body of newspaper reporters collectively
second meaning: to pester or urge someone insistently
third meaning: a dense throng of people

explanation.surface: Reporters hounding someone as a mob gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word, strung together so they read as a scene of reporters mobbing a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names reporters as a group, means to pester as a verb, and as a noun a packed throng of people.

clue.text: American game to act etc, I suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy or not right, so the preceding letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guessing a game is all about acting and so on, as in charades.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC-TAC-TOE is the American name for the game Britons call noughts and crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tic-tac-toe is the US term for noughts and crosses, played by marking Xs and Os on a three-by-three grid.

clue.text: Late extra, outstanding

parts.note: left over means extra, in excess
a payment outstanding is due

explanation.surface: A list of words about an unpaid bill: late, an extra charge, still outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed the time it was expected, so it is late.

clue.text: Aubergine in, say, good plot at end of allotment

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
G is the abbreviation for good
a plot is a scheme or plan

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener growing aubergines in a good plot at the far end of an allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land for growing vegetables in Britain; 'plot' is not land here but a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for the purple vegetable called aubergine in Britain.

clue.text: Not quite relevant, pastor getting a dog

indicators.note: not quite complete means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: germane means relevant to the matter
a pastor tends his flock, so is a shepherd of souls

explanation.surface: A vicar acquiring a dog, a fact barely relevant to anything.
explanation.walkthrough: GERMANE loses its final E to give GERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd is a breed of large working dog, also called an Alsatian.

clue.text: Saying name of dog held by lead

indicators.note: something held is gripped on both sides, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is the stock name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: Telling someone the name of the dog being held on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a dog's leash, fitting the surface, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying expressing a general truth.

clue.text: In the morning, I leave with a friend

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning
taken as written
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Someone announcing a morning departure with a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, used jokily in English.

clue.text: Won, as red put him out

indicators.note: letters put out of place are disordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooker or chess win described as the red side eliminating an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To have triumphed is to have won a victory.

clue.text: Quiz host to equestrians flummoxed about maiden

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumble wraps a single letter
someone flummoxed is thrown into confusion, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A quiz host confusing a panel of horse riders with a question about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman in the surface, but here it is the cricket term for an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A questionmaster is the person who puts the questions in a quiz, its host or presenter.

clue.text: Former cashier, reportedly in treasury

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a former one is an ex, and a cashier checks out goods

explanation.surface: A retired cashier now working in the treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: A checker is a supermarket checkout cashier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department in charge of public money, the national treasury.

clue.text: One writer, taken aback, points to antelope

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the letters run from right to left

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Biro is a ballpoint pen, so a writer

explanation.surface: An author shocked by something pointing towards an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like a person but is a pen; a Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small, slender African antelope of the grasslands.

clue.text: Have a position in partnership

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold a view on an issue
second meaning: in cricket, a run-scoring partnership between two batters

explanation.surface: Holding a post within a business partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batters, as in 'a stand of 100 runs'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a stand is to adopt a position, and cricket uses the noun for a batting partnership.

clue.text: Private compartment, say, taken by royal household officer heading off

indicators.note: with its head cut off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to say is to state
grooms, such as the Groom of the Stole, are officers of the royal household

explanation.surface: A private carriage compartment claimed by a palace official.
explanation.walkthrough: GROOM loses its G to leave ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is a private cabin on a ship or private compartment on a train.

clue.text: What could make one establish truth about female, offhand?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one letter is wrapped by the rest
the answer's letters could be made into the following words, so a rearrangement links them

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how to get at the truth concerning a woman without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble of ESTABLISH TRUTH splits around F to give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: At first blush means at first sight, without considered thought, so offhand in the sense of immediately.

clue.text: Girl with refinement almost leaves US state capital

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a girl's name
polish is refinement or elegance

explanation.surface: A cultured young woman leaving an American state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: POLISH drops its H to give POLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapolis is the capital city of Maryland, home of the US Naval Academy.

clue.text: Irrelevant, UN told

parts.note: taken as written
a story told is related

explanation.surface: The United Nations being told something is beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrelated means having no connection to the matter, so irrelevant to it.

clue.text: Free pardon daughter needed, whatever the cost?

parts.note: something free comes at no expense
to pardon someone is to spare them
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A free pardon secured for a daughter, at any price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free pardon' reads as one legal phrase, but the two words are split: free is no expense, pardon is spare.
explanation.definitionFit: No expense spared is an idiom for paying whatever is needed, regardless of the price.

clue.text: Reimburse charge for passengers and cargo

parts.note: to reimburse is to pay back
a charge is a load, as of a gun

explanation.surface: A refund of the fee charged for transporting people and goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The payload is what an aircraft or vehicle carries for revenue, its passengers and freight.

clue.text: Father's row makes one paler

parts.note: Pa is father, so Pa's
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A father's quarrel leaves someone white-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, fitting the pallor, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty means pale and unhealthy-looking, so pastier means paler.

clue.text: Monetary fund small-minded Conservative has abused

parts.note: petty means small-minded

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited Tory accused of misusing a fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty cash is the small fund of money an office keeps for minor expenses.

clue.text: Pole wearing loose outer garment in Pacific state

indicators.note: whatever is wearing a garment is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the toga was the loose robe of ancient Rome
N for the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor dressed in a loose robe in a Pacific nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: When back, boy must serve up a cold dish

indicators.note: going back means the short word is read from right to left

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy home again is told to dish up something cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad is a cold dish of raw or cooked vegetables and other ingredients.

clue.text: Drank heavily over in base

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol to excess

explanation.surface: Soldiers drinking heavily back at their base.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military base or a storage station for supplies.

clue.text: Jargon of a group from Hull in Goole

indicators.note: taken from within the following words, the letters run across their boundary

parts.note: the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: The local dialect of people from Hull living in Goole.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull and Goole are towns in Yorkshire, England, which makes regional speech plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo means the specialised vocabulary or jargon used by a particular group.

clue.text: Vegetable in cooking utensil knocked over on watch

parts.note: turnip is old slang for a large, thick pocket watch

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a pot is a cooking utensil

explanation.surface: A vegetable in a pan that gets tipped over while someone keeps an eye on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the turned-round utensil after the watch; turnip as a watch is old slang for a bulky pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnip tops are the young green leaves of the turnip, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Classic banner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a recognised model of excellence
second meaning: a flag, especially one carried in battle

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses: a classic work, and a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a classic song or work everyone knows, and also a ceremonial flag or banner.

clue.text: Put down good character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put something down to someone, attributing it to them
second meaning: a good reputation or standing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' looks like an insult, the opposite of good character, but it means to attribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit is to attribute something to someone, and credit as a noun is a good reputation or honour.
